change: Added checks #12 (constitutive-history equivalence) and #13 (initial-state equivalence). Redesigned adversarial acquisition and escalation gate per CEO Round 93.

12_constitutive_history_equivalence.description: For history-dependent materials, both solvers must produce the SAME constitutive history (stress, internal variables, tangent) over the complete loading trajectory, not just at isolated points. The entire history H(t) must match, and the stress/tangent must follow from the same update law.
12_constitutive_history_equivalence.audit_method: At each time step, compare: (a) internal variable values H_A(t) vs H_B(t), (b) stress S_A(t) vs S_B(t), (c) tangent C_A(t) vs C_B(t). All must agree to within tolerance at ALL time steps, not just sampled points.
12_constitutive_history_equivalence.tolerance: Relative difference < 1% at every time step for stress; < 2% for internal variables; < 2% for tangent
common_violations: Different update formula for internal variables (e.g., recursive vs hereditary integral)
Different time integration of the update (e.g., explicit vs implicit)
Different pull-back/push-forward operations for finite strain
Same formula but different implementation order causing accumulation of numerical error
12_constitutive_history_equivalence.applies_to: L4 (viscoelasticity), L5 (damage), and any benchmark with constitutive history

13_initial_state_equivalence.description: Both solvers must start from the SAME initial internal state. Viscoelastic models can appear identical after relaxation while starting from different internal states, producing different transient behavior.
13_initial_state_equivalence.audit_method: Verify: (a) initial values of all internal variables (H[i](0) = 0 for FEBio), (b) initial stress state (S(0) = 0), (c) initial elastic stress storage (Sep(0) = 0). Both solvers must use the same initialization.
13_initial_state_equivalence.tolerance: Exact match (all initial values must be identical)
common_violations: Different initial H (e.g., FEBio initializes H=0, SfePy initializes H=Se)
Different initial Sep (e.g., FEBio initializes Sep=0, SfePy initializes Sep=Se)
Non-zero initial conditions that produce different transients
13_initial_state_equivalence.applies_to: L4 (viscoelasticity), L5 (damage), and any benchmark with internal state variables

hard_invariant_v3_1: W_A=W_B, P_A=P_B, C_A=C_B for all F in D, AND sigma_A(t)=sigma_B(t) for all t in T, AND H_A(t)=H_B(t) for all state variables H and all t in T, AND H_A(0)=H_B(0) for all state variables

adversarial_acquisition_redesign.ceo_directive: Don't teach the AI to search where it expects to fail. Teach it to search where competing explanations make different predictions. The ideal simulation is: the cheapest experiment whose possible outcomes would most strongly distinguish my best hypothesis from its strongest surviving alternative.

old_approach_v1.problem: A candidate with 99% failure probability but low information gain can be selected over a candidate with 50% failure probability but high information gain. The product does not optimize for epistemic value.

new_approach_v2.name: Competing Hypothesis Divergence (CHD) acquisition
new_approach_v2.formula: a(x) = D_KL(p(y|x, H_best) || p(y|x, H_alt)) / cost(x)

where.D_KL: Kullback-Leibler divergence between predicted outcomes under best hypothesis and strongest alternative
where.cost(x): computational cost of simulation x (e.g., FEBio solve time in seconds)

new_approach_v2.interpretation: The AI selects the simulation that MAXIMALLY distinguishes the best hypothesis from its strongest competitor, per unit computational cost. This is the operationalization of 'competing explanations make different predictions.'
new_approach_v2.key_advantage: If H_best and H_alt predict the same outcome at x, D_KL=0, and the AI will NOT select x (no discriminating power). If they predict different outcomes, D_KL is high, and x is preferentially selected.

competing_hypothesis_engine.requirement: For every hypothesis, maintain at least 4 models:

models.supporting_model: The model that best supports the current hypothesis
models.strongest_alternative_model: The model that best supports a DIFFERENT hypothesis (the strongest competitor)
models.null_model: A model representing no effect / baseline behavior
models.failure_model: A model representing the failure mode the hypothesis claims won't happen

competing_hypothesis_engine.acquisition: Select the simulation x that maximizes the DIVERGENCE between supporting_model and strongest_alternative_model predictions. This is the experiment that most strongly distinguishes the two hypotheses.
competing_hypothesis_engine.implementation: For each candidate x, compute predicted outcome distributions under all 4 models. The acquisition value is the max pairwise KL divergence between any two models, divided by cost.

escalation_gate_redesign.ceo_directive: Replace the arbitrary '10 rounds' rule with a formal Escalation Gate based on posterior uncertainty, falsification probability, model disagreement, and cost.
escalation_gate_redesign.old_approach: Hypothesis must survive 10 adversarial simulations before physical testing
escalation_gate_redesign.problem: Ten easy simulations can be weaker evidence than two maximally discriminative experiments.

new_approach.name: Formal Escalation Gate
new_approach.trigger_condition: Escalate to physical experiment when: E[simulation_info_gain] / E[simulation_cost] < E[physical_experiment_info_gain] / E[physical_experiment_cost]

components.posterior_hypothesis_uncertainty: H[p(H|data)] — entropy of hypothesis posterior. If high, more simulations needed. If low, hypothesis is well-determined.
components.predicted_falsification_probability: P(falsification | next simulation) — if high, one more simulation could kill it. If low, hypothesis is robust.
components.solver_model_disagreement: max |FEBio(x) - SfePy(x)| / |analytical(x)| — if solvers disagree, more validation needed. If they agree, physics is settled.
components.expected_information_gain: EIG(x*) for the best candidate x* — if high, simulations are still informative. If low, diminishing returns.
components.simulation_cost: Time/cost of one more simulation (e.g., 60 seconds for FEBio)
components.physical_experiment_cost: Time/cost of one physical experiment (e.g., $10,000 and 2 weeks)

new_approach.decision_rule: escalate_to_physical = (EIG_sim / cost_sim) < (EIG_phys / cost_phys) AND solver_disagreement < threshold AND posterior_uncertainty < threshold
new_approach.rationale: The AI escalates when simulations have become less informative than reality, not when an arbitrary counter is reached. This is consistent with Article XXXIV (stop coding when reality is the next bottleneck).
